name: Antiphospholipid Syndrome - Musculoskeletal Relevance
definition: Autoimmune thrombophilia defined by clinical thrombosis or obstetric morbidity with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies; musculoskeletal relevance includes ischemic bone complications and thrombotic mimics of limb pain.

investigations.principle: Persistent antiphospholipid antibody testing plus cause-directed vascular imaging.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Anticoagulation strategy is specialist-directed; limb pain should not be assumed mechanical.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Rakta-vaha pathology may be documented only as a parallel framework.

patientEducation.summary: Autoimmune thrombophilia defined by clinical thrombosis or obstetric morbidity with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies; musculoskeletal relevance includes ischemic bone complications and thrombotic mimics of limb pain.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
